children: City Therapeutics filed a final prospectus for its initial public offering on the Nasdaq Global Market under the ticker CTY. The company is offering 11,111,111 shares at $18.00 per share, for gross proceeds of approximately $200 million, with an additional 1,666,666-share over-allotment option. Goldman Sachs, Jefferies, Stifel, and Oppenheimer are acting as underwriters, and the company qualifies as an emerging growth company.

City Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing RNA interference (RNAi) medicines designed to silence disease-causing proteins. Its platform integrates proprietary trigger engineering (including next‑generation ‘cityRNA’), ligand-based delivery for tissue selectivity, and genetics-led target selection to build highly specific and durable therapies.

The pipeline includes CITY-FXI, a GalNAc‑conjugated siRNA targeting Factor XI for thromboembolic disease prevention (in Phase 1 with initial healthy volunteer data showing up to ~85% knockdown); CITY-RBP4, a GalNAc‑conjugated siRNA for Stargardt disease (Phase 1 planned for late 2026) to reduce vitamin A transport and toxic retinal byproducts; and CITY-TFR2, a GalNAc‑conjugated siRNA for anemia of chronic disease beginning with myelofibrosis-associated anemia (IIT in China planned for late 2026 and Phase 1/2 in early 2027). Strategic collaborations with Bausch + Lomb (ocular) and Biogen (CNS) support extrahepatic delivery programs and expand the platform’s reach.
: Global anticoagulants market estimated at ~$37 billion in 2025, projected to reach ~$56 billion by 2033
: Expansion driven by broader anticoagulant use and next-generation targets like FXI
: Focused on genetically and clinically validated RNAi targets in thromboembolism, inherited retinal disease, and anemia of chronic disease
: ADARx, Bayer, Bristol-Myers Squibb, CRISPR Therapeutics/Sirius, Johnson & Johnson, Novartis, Regeneron, Alkeus, Belite Bio, Disc Medicine, Ionis, Alnylam, Arrowhead, Silence
: RNAi therapeutics expanding beyond liver targets; increasing use of GalNAc delivery; rising interest in extrahepatic delivery and long-acting subcutaneous dosing
: Pre-revenue; collaboration partners include Bausch + Lomb and Biogen
: Headquarters and R&D facilities in Cambridge, Massachusetts
: Operations in the U.S.; planned IIT in China for CITY-TFR2
: Bausch + Lomb (ocular RNAi candidate selection targeted by late 2026); Biogen (CNS RNAi candidate selection targeted by late 2027)
: 81 full-time employees as of September 1, 2026; approximately 51,726 sq. ft. of office and lab space; initial CITY-FXI SAD cohorts showed up to ~85% FXI knockdown at three weeks post 150 mg dose
, President and Chief Executive Officer - Former senior commercial leader at Alnylam and CCO at Krystal Biotech; 25+ years in biopharma launches and strategy.
, Executive Chair - Founding CEO of Alnylam for nearly 20 years; a pioneer in RNAi with leadership across multiple FDA-approved RNAi therapeutics.
, Chief Medical Officer - Led clinical development at Editas and Sanofi; key roles in approvals including ALPROLIX, ELOCTATE, ALTUVIIIO, and siRNA medicine QFITLIA.
, Chief Scientific Officer - 15 years at Alnylam; co-inventor on AMVUTTRA and co-author of landmark primate RNAi study; former CDO at Generation Bio.
, Chief Financial Officer - Former CFO at Keros Therapeutics and Wave Life Sciences; senior finance roles at Shire and Biogen; extensive capital markets experience.
, Chief Operating Officer - Company co-founder; prior operating and company creation roles at RTW Investments and Flagship Pioneering.
: Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC; Jefferies LLC; Stifel, Nicolaus & Company, Incorporated; Oppenheimer & Co. Inc.
: Approx. $30M for CITY-FXI; $20M for CITY-RBP4; $40M for CITY-TFR2; $70M for platform advancement; remainder for working capital and general corporate purposes
